verdict.rationale: Modal Sandboxes provide ephemeral, isolated environments explicitly designed to run autonomous agents and untrusted code with tools/credentials preconfigured (modal-docs-3, modal-docs-22, modal-docs-30), and community evidence shows real-world autonomous background automation built on Sandboxes (self-hosted CI runners, agent runtimes) (modal-comm-1, modal-comm-2). However, the evidence pack lacks first-class scheduling/trigger primitives (cron, webhooks, event-driven wake-up) specific to Sandboxes for hands-off background operation — automation orchestration appears to be left to the user's own code/CI setup. Missing for 10: native scheduling/trigger mechanism for sandboxes, first-party docs on long-running background job patterns, more independent case studies beyond two HN posts.
